why: Converging pointers on a sorted array, in its purest form: put one pointer at each end. If the pair sum is too small only moving the left pointer up can raise it; if too big only moving the right pointer down can lower it. Each step throws away one value for good, so the scan is O(n) with O(1) space.
hints: The array is sorted. Look at the smallest and the largest value together: what does their sum tell you if it is below the target?
If nums[lo] + nums[hi] < target, nums[lo] cannot pair with anything (hi is already the biggest partner), so lo += 1. If the sum is above target, nums[hi] is useless, so hi -= 1.
lo = 0, hi = n-1; loop while lo < hi, compare, move one pointer. Return [lo+1, hi+1] on a hit (one-based).
pitfalls: Answers are one-based positions, not zero-based indices.
Equal values like [3,3] are fine: the two pointers are different positions.
A hash map also solves it, but uses O(n) space; the sorted order is what makes O(1) possible.
